feed.summary: ATG Capital announced that Institutional Shareholder Services Inc. (ISS) has recommended that Empery Digital Inc. stockholders vote for two of ATG Capital's nominees, Gabriel D. Gliksberg and Aaron T. Morris, to the Empery Digital Board of Directors. ISS also advised withholding support from incumbent directors Orn Olason and Ian Read and voting against the company's equity incentive plan at the upcoming October 14, 2026, Annual Meeting. feed.title: American Airlines Says Downgraded Business Class Passengers on International Flights Aren't Entitled to a Partial Refund: A Couple Want the DOT to Force it to Change
feed.summary: A Tennessee couple, downgraded from Business Class to Premium Economy on an American Airlines international flight, is pursuing legal action and petitioning the DOT to mandate partial cash refunds for downgraded passengers. American Airlines argues it's not obligated to provide compensation under the Montreal Convention, despite a court already siding with the couple once. The Taylors are seeking not only their own compensation but also retroactive payouts for all similarly affected passengers since 2024.

feed.title: Coca-Cola Southwest completes $42 million expansion of San Antonio bottling plant

The expansion adds 170,000 square feet, a second production line, and increased warehouse space to manage demand fluctuations. The San Antonio plant currently employs nearly 900 people.

feed.title: Coca-Cola Names Rob Gehring President of North America Operating Unit
feed.summary: The Coca-Cola Company has appointed Rob Gehring as president of its North America operating unit, effective December 1, 2026. Gehring, who previously served as CEO, Americas, at Monster Energy Company, brings extensive experience from his earlier career at Coca-Cola and other beverage companies. He succeeds John Murphy, who will continue in his role as Coca-Cola’s president and chief financial officer.

feed.title: Azure’s Inflection Point: Can Microsoft (MSFT) Balance AI Growth With Capex Risk?
feed.summary: Microsoft (MSFT) stock has underperformed the broader market due to concerns about increasing capital expenditures, particularly in AI infrastructure. Despite these positive indicators, risks remain, including high capital requirements, intense AI competition, and uncertainties surrounding Copilot's monetization.
